summary: IbisBackend — the primary public entry point for all Ibis-backed relational database connections. Accepts three input forms: settings (SettingsParameters), URL string, or dialect+kwargs. connect() returns self (fluent). IbisConnection wraps the live ibis backend object and exposes the standard inspection API. Full DDL/DML surface: create_table, drop_table, create_view, insert, truncate, upsert (dialect-hooked), create_index, drop_index, list_indexes, rename_table, run_sql, run_expr, to_sql.
extension_points: Capability hooks: upsert_hook, create_index_hook, drop_index_hook, rename_table_hook — per-dialect in DialectSpec
ibis_connection() escapes the abstraction for advanced ibis-native operations
lifecycle_notes: Three construction paths: positional SettingsParameters, positional URL string, keyword dialect=.
Fluent: connect()/close() return self — supports chaining and context manager use.
upsert, create_index, drop_index, rename_table raise NotImplementedError if the dialect DialectSpec has no hook.
index_exists and list_indexes import mountainash — creates an implicit dependency on the mountainash meta-package.
documentation_hooks: Three construction forms deserve a dedicated 'how to connect' page
MotherDuck URL special-case (duckdb://md:) should be called out explicitly
Fluent interface pattern (connect().list_tables()) vs context manager deserve comparison examples
risks: index_exists and list_indexes have an implicit dependency on mountainash meta-package (import mountainash as ma) — may break if mountainash is not installed
IbisConnection.list_namespaces uses print() for errors instead of logging
open_questions: Should IbisBackend implement the Backend protocol formally (isinstance check)?

evidence.detail: class IbisBackend with name='ibis' and full DDL/DML surface
